turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Priya, Sara at HyperSale—could I take 30 seconds? I’m calling because freight teams use us to reduce ramp-time attrition through realistic buyer practice.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: You’ve got 30 seconds. What do you mean by realistic buyer practice?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Reps roleplay with AI buyers modeled on freight objections, then managers see scores tied to exact quotes. Where are new hires struggling most today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: It’s less freight knowledge than not knowing early who’s coachable before they miss quota. We already do ride-alongs, though.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That makes sense—ride-alongs help, but your issue is getting an earlier, consistent signal. How long does it take today to identify an uncoachable hire?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Usually not until they’ve missed quota and a manager’s already sunk a lot of time into them. I’m not convinced an AI roleplay tells me who’s actually coachable, though.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Fair concern—it shouldn’t replace judgment. If weekly practice showed who applies feedback, how many hires could you flag before they miss quota?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Maybe two or three a quarter. But we bought Gong and nobody used it, so why would this be any different?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Fair—if Gong became shelfware, another tool is a bad bet. What specifically kept reps and managers from using it?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Reps saw it as surveillance, and managers never built it into their coaching cadence. After a month, usage fell off.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s the real risk: without a coaching cadence, any tool becomes shelfware. How are your managers coaching today, and what would reps willingly practice?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Mostly ride-alongs and deal reviews once something’s already going wrong. I don’t have time to build a whole new coaching program around another tool.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: You shouldn’t have to build one. If we fit a 30-day pilot into one manager’s existing deal review, what would prove it saves time?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: If it showed within the first few weeks who was actually applying feedback, without adding more than 15 minutes to the manager’s weekly review, that’d be meaningful. What does a pilot like that cost?
